title: Invertibility of the canonical right-adjoint mate along an affine open
statement: Let f:X→Y be proper, flat, and locally of finite presentation, with Y qcqs. Fix derived categories on every scheme, a right adjoint a to the canonical lifted direct image of f, and its adjunction. Let V be an affine open of Y and choose any right adjoint aV to the lifted derived direct image pullback(f,V→Y)→V, with its adjunction. Suppose the canonical ordinary derived base-change maps for f along V→Y are isomorphisms on every quasi-coherent derived object. For every K in D_QCoh(Y), the ambient canonical right-adjoint mate Lp* a(K)→aV(LV* K) is an isomorphism. The scheme, pullback, categories, direct images, ordinary base change and canonical mate are [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image, lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint, def-pc-derived-base-change-map, def-sc-duality-equation-base-change-map]; properness and flatness are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: Use pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict to identify the canonical pullback along V with U=f inverse(V). The canonical derived pullback along either open inclusion identifies with exact open restriction. Derived direct-image composition and the uniqueness of right adjoints transport the supplied aV and adjV to the right adjoint of the restricted f.

Expand the fixed canonical mate into the pullback of a applied to the open unit, the pullback of the inverse conjugate of ordinary base change, and the open pullback counit. Both latter factors are invertible, the former by hbeta0 and conjugateEquiv_iso and the latter by full faithfulness of open pushforward. The open counit and triangle identities give the sheafy map of Tag 0E4G and identify its first factor with the restricted unit in proper_flat_rightAdjoint_restriction_open.

An affine open is quasi-compact. Apply proper_flat_rightAdjoint_restriction_open to f and V and the derived open adjunction to get invertibility of the first factor. Multiply the three isomorphisms and transport through the comparisons to conclude invertibility of the ambient canonical mate at K.
